LanguageData.Planetsmith_EnableOverhaulTip: When on, Planetsmith recomputes each tile's temperature, rainfall, and biome from its own climate model during world generation. When off, worlds generate as vanilla.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_ControlSeaLevelDefaultTip: When on, Planetsmith raises or lowers sea level during world generation until the planet has the land fraction set below. Leave off to let vanilla, or another mod, decide the coastline.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_ShowMapModeButton: Show map-mode button on the planet view
LanguageData.Planetsmith_ShowMapModeButtonTip: Adds a button to the planet view for shading the world by temperature, rainfall and Planetsmith's other climate layers.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_DefaultsNote: These are the defaults new planets start from. To shape one planet, use the Planetsmith button on the world creation page.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_WorldParametersIntro: These apply to the world you are about to generate.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_ControlSeaLevelTip: When on, Planetsmith raises or lowers sea level until the planet has the land fraction set below. Leave off to let vanilla, or another mod, decide the coastline.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_SeaLevelRivalNote: {0} also sets sea level. Planetsmith runs afterwards, so this setting wins; turn it off to leave the coastline to {0}.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_AxialTiltExternal: Axial tilt: set by Realistic Axial Tilt
LanguageData.Planetsmith_AxialTiltExternalNote: Realistic Axial Tilt is installed, so the tilt slider on the world creation page sets it for both mods. Planetsmith builds the biomes around the temperatures it works out, so what you generate matches what you play.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_AxialTiltExplanation: Tilt is why a planet has seasons. Upright worlds barely change through the year; steeply tilted ones swing between harsh summers and winters.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_WorldbuilderTiltNote: Worldbuilder has its own axial tilt, which sets how far temperatures swing through the year once you are playing. This one decides how the seasons shape the planet's biomes while it is generated. They are separate, so set both the same way if you want the world to match how it plays.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_WorldbuilderBiomesNote: Worldbuilder's own biome menu offers the same two controls, and both are applied, so you can use either. This one leaves out sea, lake and ice, which have no dry-land alternative and would leave a planet unable to draw if they were turned off.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_ClimateTuningIntro: These adjust the simulation for the world you are about to generate. Left at their defaults they change nothing.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_GlobalTemperatureTip: Warms or cools the whole planet before anything else is worked out.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_ElevationCoolingTip: How much colder high ground becomes. Higher values put snow on smaller mountains.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_RainfallScaleTip: Scales the rain falling everywhere, before mountains, coasts and monsoons have their say.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_RainShadowTip: How thoroughly mountains wring out the air crossing them. Air stripped harder stays dry further inland, so this sets how far a shadow reaches as well as how dry it is.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_MoistureReachTip: How far sea air carries its water before running dry. Higher values green the interiors.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_MonsoonStrengthTip: How heavy the seasonal rains are on tropical coasts.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_SeasonIntensityTip: How far temperatures swing between summer and winter, which decides where frost-shy biomes can live.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_CoastalInfluenceTip: How strongly the sea tempers the coasts beside it, mild where the wind comes off the water and cold and dry where it does not.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_BiomesIntro: Turn a biome off to keep it off this planet. Frequency scales how much ground it takes where the climate already suits it; offset nudges it into or out of places it narrowly loses or wins.
LanguageData.Planetsmith_MapModesTip: Shade the planet by the climate Planetsmith generated for it.
